t.3.70.1: Those two sons of the best of men, taking the western direction, set out in the forest upon that path to Pampā which Kabandha had shown them.
t.3.70.3: Having made their dwelling on the mountain's slope, those two delights of the Raghus, the Rāghavas, then approached the western shore of Pampā.
t.3.70.2: Those two, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, set out to see Sugrīva, gazing as they went at the countless trees crowded upon the mountains, their fruits as sweet as honey.
t.3.70.4: The two of them reached the western shore of the lotus-lake Pampā, and then they saw there the delightful hermitage of Śabarī.
t.3.70.5: Reaching that hermitage, surrounded by many trees and exceedingly lovely, the two gazed about it and approached Śabarī.
t.3.70.6: Then, seeing the two of them, the perfected ascetic woman rose up with joined palms and clasped the feet of Rāma and of the wise Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.70.7: Then Rāma spoke to her, the female ascetic of firm vows: "Have your obstacles been overcome? Does your austerity flourish?"
t.3.70.8: O ascetic lady, I hope your anger and your food are held in check? I hope you have kept your vows, and that your mind is at ease? I hope, O sweet-spoken one, that your service to your teachers has borne fruit?
t.3.70.9: Questioned by Rāma, the aged ascetic Śabarī, a woman of spiritual perfection esteemed by the Siddhas, who stood before Rāma, spoke to him in reply.
t.3.70.10: When you reached Citrakūṭa, those whom I used to serve rose from here to heaven in celestial chariots of matchless splendor.
t.3.70.11: And I was told by those great sages, knowers of dharma and highly blessed: "Rāma will come to this most holy hermitage of yours."
t.3.70.12: He, accompanied by Saumitri, is a guest who must be received by you; and having seen him, you will go to the excellent, imperishable worlds.
t.3.70.13: But I have gathered for your sake, O bull among men, O tiger among men, various forest produce grown on the banks of the Pampā.
t.3.70.16: Having heard these words that had issued from Rāma's mouth, Śabarī showed the two of them that great forest.
t.3.70.15: From Danu I have heard truly of your power, great-souled lady; that which I have heard I wish to see with my own eyes, if you think fit.
t.3.70.14: Thus addressed by Śabarī, the righteous-souled Rāghava said this to Śabarī: “I know her to be one who has never been cast out.”
t.3.70.17: Behold, O Raghunandana, this forest that looks like a dense mass of clouds and teems with beasts and birds; it is renowned by the name Mataṃgavana.
t.3.70.18: Here, O greatly radiant one, those teachers of mine, of purified souls, made offerings into the sacred fire with mantras, at this holy place honored by mantras.
t.3.70.19: This is the western altar, where those whom I held in deep honor make offerings of flowers with hands trembling from weariness.
t.3.70.20: See, O best of the Raghus, how even today, by the power of their austerities, the altars of incomparable radiance light up all the directions with their splendour.
t.3.70.21: Behold the seven oceans gathered together here, which came at the mere thought of them, who, languid from the weariness of fasting, were unable to go to them.
t.3.70.22: O Raghunandana, the bark garments that they placed here on the trees after performing their ablutions have still not dried in this place, even today.
t.3.70.23: This entire forest has been seen by you, and what was to be heard has been heard by you. Therefore, with your permission, I wish to abandon this body.
t.3.70.24: I wish to go into the presence of those sages of purified souls, whose hermitage this is and whom I served as an attendant.
t.3.70.25: Having heard these most righteous words, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, his face beaming with joy, said, "I give you leave; go."
t.3.70.26: Permitted by Rāma, she offered herself as an oblation into the fire, and, resembling a blazing fire, she went to heaven itself.
t.3.70.27: Through deep absorption of the self, Śabarī went to that holy realm where those great sages of virtuous soul dwell and roam in delight.
